claims.text: The multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy initially has a native protective oxide film.
Mechanical wear disrupts the alloy's protective oxide film.
Disruption of the oxide film exposes fresh alloy surfaces.
Freshly exposed alloy surfaces corrode more rapidly because they lack passivation.
Wear-induced oxide disruption enhances localized corrosion rates.
Corrosion products may weaken the surface.
Corrosion-induced surface weakening increases the wear rate.
The interaction between wear and corrosion is synergistic.
Total material loss under simultaneous wear and corrosion will be greater than the sum of losses measured under independent wear-only and corrosion-only exposure.
The wear rate under simultaneous wear and corrosion will exceed the wear-only baseline.
The corrosion rate under simultaneous wear and corrosion will exceed the corrosion-only baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies only where protective oxide formation is possible and both wear and corrosion are active.
The proposed mechanism does not apply when protective oxide films are absent or either wear or corrosion is negligible.
The magnitude of the synergistic effect depends on alloy composition, oxide-film stability, and environmental severity.

contradictions.description: The baseline calls for a wear-only sample at the same corrosive environment as the coupled test. If wear occurs in an active corrosive medium, that sample is itself under simultaneous wear and corrosion rather than a true wear-only control. The experimental design does not resolve this control-environment inconsistency.
